newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end mostly up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end mostly up on short-covering.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed firmer on Thursday, with the exception of the spot November contract, helped by private investors' short-covering, traders said.
Prices were up to 210 yen firmer.
Benchmark September finished up 210 yen at 16,400 yen per tonne. Volume was 68,108 lots.

A growing view that the market was oversold prompted investors to cover shorts for most of the day, the traders said. "But technical factors in the market have not improved much, which should put a lid on price rallies," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
The spot September contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $3.55 per bushel at 0820 GMT, against its $3.55-1/2 Wednesday close.
September CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system were at $8.16-1/4 at 0823 GMT, against $8.19-1/2 at Wednesday's close.
